key_insight: HTP-Net improves counting and boundary precision for dense welding stubs by combining high-resolution edge preservation, global topology modeling, and orientation-aware instance segmentation.
engineering_relevance: The method directly supports industrial warehouse metrology and automated inventory management for welding consumables in real factory settings.
method: Wavelet-Driven Edge-Preserving module retains subtle boundaries during downsampling
Long-Range Topology Representation Block uses global context to reduce breaks in slender object masks
Orientation-Driven Instance Segmentation Head exploits rotation priors to suppress overlap and NMS errors
evidence_signal: On custom and public dense-slender-target datasets, the model improved mAP@50 by at least 1.2% and up to 55.3%, and the deployed factory system reported 99% accuracy for electrodes and 94% for wire stubs.
watch_item: Performance is strong, but deployment may still depend on stable imaging conditions and careful calibration for highly occluded or visually degraded stubs.
paper_title: High-resolution topology-preserving instance segmentation network for vision-based measurement system of dense welding material stubs
